questions.question: How do you define and use custom exceptions in Ruby?
questions.title: Custom Exceptions in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: To make a custom exception, define a class that inherits from StandardError (or a more specific built-in): class PaymentError < StandardError; end. You raise it with raise PaymentError, 'card declined' (the message is in e.message) and rescue it by class: rescue PaymentError => e. Custom exceptions let callers rescue YOUR error specifically, not a generic StandardError, so the handler can act on the real cause. Keep them under StandardError (not Exception) so they're caught by default rescue and don't capture signals. You can add fields (attr_reader :order_id) by overriding initialize.

sections.title: Your Own Error Class
sections.content: To make a custom exception, define a class that inherits from StandardError, or a more specific built-in: class PaymentError less-than StandardError, end. You raise it with raise PaymentError, card declined, and the message is in e dot message, and rescue it by class: rescue PaymentError arrow e. Custom exceptions let callers rescue YOUR error specifically, not a generic StandardError, so the handler can act on the real cause instead of guessing. Keep them under StandardError, not Exception, so they're caught by the default rescue and don't capture signals. You can add fields like attr_reader order_id by overriding initialize to take extra data.

sections.title: Define -> Raise -> Rescue
sections.content:
class X < StandardError; raise X, msg; rescue X => e.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  D[class PaymentError < StandardError] --> R[raise PaymentError, 'declined']
  R --> C[rescue PaymentError => e]
  C --> H[handle the real cause]
```

sections.title: Custom exceptions
sections.content:
```ruby
# Define a custom exception (inherit from StandardError!)
class PaymentError < StandardError
  attr_reader :order_id
  def initialize(msg, order_id: nil)
    super(msg)                 # set the message
    @order_id = order_id        # extra context
  end
end

# Raise it with a message and context:
def charge(order)
  raise PaymentError.new('card declined', order_id: order.id) if order.failed?
end

# Rescue it specifically by class:
begin
  charge(order)
rescue PaymentError => e
  logger.error("payment failed for #{e.order_id}: #{e.message}")
  # handler acts on the REAL cause, not a generic StandardError
end

# Keep it under StandardError (NOT Exception) so default rescue catches it.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Inheriting from Exception (not StandardError) — won't be caught by default rescue.
Rescuing a generic StandardError instead of the specific class (can't act on cause).
Forgetting super(msg) in initialize (the message won't be set).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: A custom exception is a class inheriting from StandardError (or a specific built-in).
raise X, 'msg' raises it; the message is in e.message (call super(msg) if you add fields).
rescue X => e rescues it specifically so the handler acts on the real cause.
Keep under StandardError (not Exception) so default rescue catches it.
Add fields (attr_reader :order_id) by overriding initialize and calling super(msg).
